newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish demonstrate against Islamist surge.
newsitem.headline: Turkish demonstrate against Islamist surge.

text.p: Several thousand Turkish women took to the streets of the capital on Saturday in a protest march against a surge of Islamist activity by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party.
Protesters chanted "No to Sharia (Islamic law)" and "Join hands for democracy" as a women's demonstration through the centre of Ankara got under way in light rain.
Some carried posters of Kemal Ataturk, the secularist founder of modern Turkey who gave women the vote in the 1920s and encouraged them to throw away the Islamic veil.
Women's groups and the opposition have accused Erbakan and his party of trying to chip away at Turkey's official secularism with a series of Islamist proposals.
Welfare has recently called for the construction of big mosques in traditionally secularist districts, and overland pilgrimages to the Moslem holy city of Mecca in Saudi Arabia.
But the party, under pressure from its pro-Western coalition partners, has shelved a plan to lift a ban on female public employees wear Islamic headscarves.
A Welfare party former mayor was charged this week with serious public order offences for organising an anti-Israeli protest.
